(A) Axial CT of the abdomen obtained in the portal venous phase following intravenous contrast material administration shows a hypoenhancing mass in the body of the pancreas (white arrow) with multiple hypoenhancing liver metastases (one indicated by the black arrow). Characteristically, neuroendocrine tumors hyperenhance in the arterial phase following contrast administration but hypoenhancing lesions do occur. The tail of the pancreas upstream of the tumor is hypoenhancing due to obstructive pancreatitis related to the tumor.
in_text_mentions: e larger pancreatic NETs may demonstrate cystic areas or calcifications (127). Multi-phasic CT or MRI are the standard imaging modalities used to diagnose pancreatic NETs (135, 136). Pancreatic NETs characteristically show homogeneous, hyperintense enhancement on CT or MRI following contrast administration (137) (Figures 6, 7). Larger, malignant pancreatic NETs are often heterogeneous with non-enhancing cystic components and solid enhancing components located at the periphery (127). On MRI, lesions are usually hypointense on T1 weighted imaging and hyperintense on T2 weighted imaging (8, 138).

in_text_mentions: The patient underwent an endoscopic ultrasound (EUS), which identified a 1.4 cm × 1.2 cm well-defined hyperechoic rounded mass in the head of pancreas, with an adjacent focus of calcification ( Figure 1 ). The rest of the pancreas looked atrophied. Fine needle aspiration (FNA) and biopsy of the mass were performed.

A: Panel A is a CT scan showing a 10-mm enhancing lesion in the pancreatic body, consistent with an insulinoma as described in the caption and text. B: Panel B shows mesenteric nodules supplied by the accessory middle colic artery, described as corresponding to mesenteric metastases of the insulinoma. C: Panel C shows additional hypervascular mesenteric foci, continuing the metastatic disease presentation of the insulinoma.
